text:
alex: Quick sync — I'm worried our current hard-tier routing (pin to tier until capacity exhausted) is causing latency cliffs during bursts. Should we consider a soft-preference model that blends latency, cost, and remaining quota?

maria: +1. Hard pins are simple but brittle. We saw a tenant OOM when their Dedicated pool hit a short-lived spike.

devon: Thoughts: soft preference = score(route) = base_score - penalty(capacity) - penalty(latency) + bonus(region_affinity). Then pick top N with hedging.

sasha: Important: any scoring must be explainable for SRE. We need deterministic tie-breaks and a way to lock a tenant to previous model during rollout.

linh: Agreed. Also need to avoid per-request heavy calc. We can precompute score buckets per-minute and read from a cache.

patrick: +1 cache idea. Implementation question: do we expose the scoring DSL to product teams or keep it internal?

maria: Keep DSL internal for now. Expose config knobs: region_pref, latency_sensitivity, cost_cap_pct. That should cover 90% of use cases without UI plumbing.

alex: Example pseudo-DSL we discussed earlier:
```
policy "soft_pref" {
  prefer { region: "us-east", weight: 0.6 }
  penalties {
    capacity: { type: "sigmoid", slope: 0.12 }
    p99_latency_ms: { threshold: 150, weight: 0.5 }
  }
  hedging { windows: 2, candidate_count: 3 }
  fallback { cost_cap: 0.08, region_fallback: true }
}
```
This would let runtime compute a numeric score and do top-k hedged routing.

devon: Two followups: (1) how do we guarantee SLA tiers? If soft pref moves some traffic off a tenant's Dedicated pool to a cheaper shared model, SLA could be violated. (2) how to simulate?

sasha: For (1) we should have hard constraints that override scores. E.g., if tenant_has_sla == true then routes must satisfy latency_sla and isolation_flag. Scores only apply to eligible routes.

linh: For (2) we can reuse the policy-sim infra. Run a weekend replay with realistic burst traces and compute expected p99 & cost delta. We should also add a "min-preserved-capacity" constraint to the sim.

patrick: Ops question: how does cache invalidation work when backend capacity changes? We need a cheap signal to bump bucket version.

devon: Emit a short-lived version stamp from capacity manager on any scale event. The router reads version per-tenant and invalidates score cache for that tenant. Very cheap.

maria: Edge case: region failover during outage. Soft pref might slowly bleed traffic into another region. We want faster migration if latency rises > X% in a short window. Add a momentum term in the scoring to accelerate region switches.

alex: I like momentum. Implementation: track exponential moving average of p99 delta, if ema > threshold then add large penalty to current routes.

sasha: Also need observability: expose per-tenant routing decisions and contributing score components in the console (top 3 factors). Otherwise triage is painful.

linh: That data is heavy. We should sample 1% of requests for full score breakdown and aggregate at 1m granularity. Store metrics keyed by tenant+policy_id.

patrick: Security/compliance note: Private deployments must be able to opt-out of cross-region fallbacks. Add policy boolean allow_cross_region_fallback.

alex: Good call. Also reminder: any change needs a canary rollout path. We should implement a safe rollout plan: preview (sim only) -> low-volume canary -> tenant opt-in -> global flip.

maria: Can we add a "predictive headroom" metric from capacity manager to reduce false positives when autoscaler is about to add nodes? If headroom incoming > 20% in next 30s, lower capacity penalty.

devon: Yes, capacity-manager can publish "capacity_horizon" events. Router can consume and adjust penalty curve.

sasha: Minor UX thing: include a reason code in route decisions so customer support can see "reason: momentum_region_failover" or "reason: cost_saving_fallback".

linh: Implementation note: keep reason codes short and enumerable. They should map cleanly into the console and logs.

patrick: Does anyone object to us starting a small RFC for this with API sketches + sim plan? I can draft operations playbook for rollbacks.

alex: No objections. Please include these acceptance criteria:
- deterministic scoring with tie-break rules
- hard-constraint bypass for SLA/Isolation
- precompute/cache per-tenant buckets, invalidated by version stamp
- sample-based score telemetry + aggregates in console
- rollout plan: sim -> canary -> opt-in -> global
- reason codes + observability in support flows

maria: I'll open the RFC draft and add a simulation checklist.

deploy-bot: :information_source: canary rollout started for policy-sim infra (build/789). Notify #eng-runtime on anomalies.
